translations.text: And when fifty years had passed in this state since the coming of Marwan the Deaf, Chichnaom, son of Muhammad, came again.
He laid waste and destroyed every settlement of Kartli, and he set out to enter Kakheti, so that he might lay it waste and leave it entirely without inhabitants.
The kings, the princes and all the people were in great fear, and they could not resist him,
For ever since the Deaf one had ruined this land, it had not yet returned to its former state, even though long periods had passed in peace.
Then the holy Archil resolved in his heart, out of the courage of his heart,
to go to him and see him, and to ask him for peace for the land, for the churches to be kept undisturbed, and for the people to be spared pressure to abandon their faith.
Trusting in God, he chose to lay down his own life and soul as a ransom for the Christians. He rose and went to Chichanaom, who was called Asim.
When he learned that Archil was coming, he went out to meet him with joy and greeted him with great honour. And they spent that day together.
He praised his goodness, and he was delighted by his fine stature and above all by the beauty of his face.
And after a few days he began to speak with flattery. He promised him great gifts and urged him to abandon the faith of Christ and convert, becoming a Saracen.
But the holy Archil would not accept his deceit at all. With a steadfast mind he answered him and said:
"Far be it from me to listen to your words, or to abandon Christ, the living God, who is the true God," who endured death in the flesh for our salvation.
"And if I listen to you, know that I would die a death by which I would be tormented for ever."
But if you kill me, I will rise again like my God and will also be glorified with him."
When the lawless man heard all this and saw his unwavering steadfastness, he was greatly amazed.
He ordered him to be seized and placed in prison, so that he might win him over by some scheme. For he did not want him to die, because of the beauty of his appearance and his tall stature.
And when they had brought him into the prison, he blessed God and asked for his help,
that in his mercy he might make him worthy to attain and inherit the never-ending light with all the saints who gained immortality by dying for God's sake.
Then a certain prince from Gardabani, who had converted to the Saracens, came before Asim.
[?] His paternal uncle had been killed by the Tsanars, and his killers had escaped safely to Archil's grandfather, King Adarnase.
For this reason, then, the man of Gardabani bore a grudge, and he said to Asim: "Do you not know who this Archil is?
He is the son of Stephen and a kinsman of the great king Vakhtang, who was of the line of Mirian, son of Chosroes.
He was with his father when they buried the royal treasures of Kartli. He also knows
He is the one with whom [?] King Heraclius buried his treasure, for Heraclius showed him where they were burying it."
When Asim heard this, he summoned Archil again and said to him: "Before, I looked on you with favour because of your fine appearance, for you are very handsome.
But now I have been told about you that you are a son of the great Khosroid kings. So now you will be exalted all the more in my sight
if you listen to me. Your kingdom will remain your own, and I will also grant you the treasures of your fathers.
First show me the treasuries of the kings of the Greeks, and convert to my faith.
Become a Saracen, and I will make you spasalar (commander-in-chief) over the land of Kartli, king and lord over the peoples of Kartli."
Then the holy Archil answered: "Know for certain that I was young when King Heraclius passed through this land.
But my father and my brother placed all their treasures in that fortress from which the Deaf emir turned back.
"And now the Greeks hold it. But I will not abandon the Lord my God, nor will I sell that unfading glory for this one, which passes away so quickly."
Asim answered and said to him: "Were you, then, present at that defeat of the Saracens in Abkhazia?"
Saint Archil said to him: "I was there at the time when God struck them down." Asim said to him: "Which God struck down the Saracens?"
Saint Archil answered and said to him: "The living God, who is the Creator of heaven and earth, and who came down from heaven to earth for the salvation of the human race,
and by his own death raised us up and granted us immortality. It was he who struck them down and humbled them."
Asim said to Saint Archil: "Since your God is mortal, and you place your hope of life in a mortal, it is fitting that you too should die."
And he ordered that Saint Archil be put to death by beheading. He did not spare him for his goodness, nor did he hold back out of respect for the glory of his high rank.
They led him outside and cut off his head with a sword in the month of Mirhkani, which is March.
And he committed his soul into the hands of the Creator, choosing the death that brings immortality.
And he exchanged this short-lived earthly kingship for eternal joy,
He was found worthy to stand before God among the ranks of the saints and valiant martyrs, and with them, wearing a crown, he rejoices before the Holy Trinity.

Now when the holy martyr Archil had been put to death, the Goderdziani of Tbeti came that night, and with them other nobles of the Mamean [?] family, and they stole away the body of the holy martyr Archil.
They carried it off, [?] it with great honour (the text has "shattered/crushed", probably a corruption, perhaps for "clothed" or "adorned"), and buried it at Notkora, in the church that he had built.
And his wife granted villages in Kakheti as hereditary estates to those who had brought back the body of the holy martyr Archil.
This book of his martyrdom was found written down only briefly [?], because in the times of turmoil no one had been able to write it down properly.
